The noun developed partly from the adjective and partly from the corresponding French noun {{m|fr|rond}}. {{dbt|en|rotund}}. ====Adjective==== [[File:Round Objects.jpg|thumb|Various round objects]] {{en-adj}} {{en-adj|er,more}} # {{lb|en|physical}} {{n-g|Of shape:}} ## [[circular|Circular]] or [[cylindrical]]; having a [[circular]] cross-section in one direction. ##: {{uxa|en|We sat at a '''round''' table to make conversation easier.}} ##* {{RQ:Tolkien Fellowship of the Ring|chapter=A Long-Expected Party|passage=The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians{{sic}} trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the '''round''' windows.}} ## [[spherical|Spherical]]; shaped like a [[ball]]; having a [[circular]] cross-section in more than one direction. ##: {{uxa|en|The ancient Egyptian demonstrated that the Earth is '''round''', not flat.}} ## Loosely or approximately circular. ##: {{coa|en|a '''round''' belly}} ##: {{coa|en|a '''round''' face}} ##* {{RQ:Christie Autobiography|II|2|passage=If I close my eyes I can see Marie today as I saw her then. '''Round''', rosy face, snub nose, dark hair piled up in a chignon.}} ## {{U|plump}}. ##: {{uxa|en|He was tall and thin but his wife was short and '''round'''.}} # {{U|complete}}, [[whole]], not lacking. #: {{uxa|en|The baker sold us a '''round''' dozen.}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson Idylls|page=47|passage='''Round''' was their pace at first, but slackened soon: / A stranger meeting them had surely
